narrative:
The model determined that you have a 71% probability of representing a bad credit risk. This high likelihood led directly to the denial of your loan application.

The decision was driven primarily by three key aspects of your profile. Most influential was the status of your checking account, which is currently in negative balance. This is relatively uncommon—only 12.6% of approved applicants show a negative balance, while most maintain either no account or positive funds. This factor strongly pushed the prediction toward bad credit risk.

The purpose of the loan, a request to finance a new car, was the second most important element. While not uncommon, this purpose appeared less frequently among successfully approved applications compared to requests for radio/TV or furniture.

Third, the duration of the requested credit—24 months—is noticeably longer than the average of about 19 months seen among approved applicants. This longer repayment period also contributed to the model's assessment of higher risk.

Taken together, these elements created enough concern that the bank could not approve the application. 

To improve your chances in the future, focus first on bringing your checking account balance back into positive territory and maintaining it there for several months. Consider applying for a shorter loan term or exploring alternative purposes that better align with patterns of successful applications. Once your account status improves, reapply and you may receive a more favorable decision. (218 words)
